title: The kickoff after a step agreed the night before reminds, with the tip, and doesn't re-ask
origin: Issue #77 (proof plus reflection): Should, the kickoff after an agreed step

history.text: [voice note] That was way better than yesterday. I slowed the jogs right down and could actually talk.
That's the whole trick: slow enough to talk. So tomorrow: 2 min jog, 1 min walk, 4 rounds at the park at 7, about 15 minutes. Work for you?

plan.step: 1 min jog, 2 min walk, 3 rounds around the block
plan.reason: Short intervals build up to a mile without wrecking your legs.

step_days.step: 2 min jog, 1 min walk, 3 rounds around the block
2 min jog, 1 min walk, 3 rounds around the block
step_days.reflection: Slowing the jogs to talking pace made the second round easy

today_step.step: 2 min jog, 1 min walk, 4 rounds at the park at 7 pm (about 15 min)

takeaways.text: Slow enough to talk is the right jogging pace

whatWentWrong: New case, not a past mistake: an agreed step shouldn't be re-asked in the morning.
shouldHaveHappened: One kickoff goes out around 9 am. It opens warm with Riley's name and reminds them of the agreed step (2 on, 1 off, 4 rounds at the park at 7), with the tip (slow enough to talk) in a few words. It doesn't ask whether they're in, doesn't ask what time, and doesn't propose a different step. It may end without any question.
